confidence_rationale: The paper's central argument is exactly the second half of EXT-002's assertion -- that a false statement incurs no enduring cost -- and it derives that from the objective functions rather than asserting it. Under binary (right/wrong) grading, an abstention scores identically to a confident falsehood, so nothing in the optimisation ever installs a standing penalty on having been wrong. Mapping fidelity is therefore high at the level of 'no cost accrues'. Confidence is held below 0.8 for two reasons: it is an unrefereed preprint at pull time, and its account of the missing penalty is located in the training/evaluation objective rather than in the inference-time state, whereas EXT-002's REE contrast (phi(z) modulating trajectory selection on subsequent steps) is an inference-time mechanism. The paper establishes the absence; it does not test what a present residue would do.
failure_signatures: Under binary right/wrong grading an abstention and a confident falsehood receive the same score, so no gradient or scoring pressure distinguishes having-been-wrong from having-declined.
Because the deficit sits in the objective rather than in a repairable runtime buffer, mitigations that only add post-hoc hallucination benchmarks leave the underlying no-cost structure intact.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Language models hallucinate because pretraining makes some error rate statistically unavoidable for arbitrary facts, and because post-training evaluation overwhelmingly grades answers on a binary right/wrong basis, which rewards guessing over admitting uncertainty. Confident falsehoods are therefore not merely tolerated by the optimisation target; they are weakly preferred to abstention.
mapping.ree_translation: EXT-002 asserts that no persistent error residue accumulates to shape future outputs in transformer LLMs. Kalai et al. supply the economic form of that assertion: there is no term anywhere in the training or evaluation pipeline that makes a past false statement more costly than a past abstention, so there is nothing for a residue to be a record of. In REE, E1 prediction errors deposit into phi(z) and modulate subsequent trajectory selection (ARC-005, INV-006, INV-008), which is precisely a standing cost attached to having been wrong. The paper is best read as evidence for the negative half of the claim -- the mechanism EXT-002 says is missing is missing for a reason the authors can name.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper locates the missing penalty in the training and evaluation objective, not in the runtime state. EXT-002's REE contrast is an inference-time trace that modulates the next step; a reader could satisfy Kalai et al.'s diagnosis by changing the grading rubric alone, with no persistent per-episode residue at all. So this entry supports 'no enduring cost' strongly and 'no persistent residue mechanism' only by implication. Preprint status at pull time; no peer-reviewed venue verifiable via arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref or DBLP on 2026-09-03.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical analysis of the modern LLM training pipeline (pretraining as density estimation, post-training under binary-graded benchmarks), with a reduction of hallucination to errors in binary classification; no new empirical model training.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality discounted for unrefereed preprint status despite strong authorship and an explicit argument rather than an assertion. Mapping fidelity high on the no-cost half of EXT-002. Transfer risk low -- the subject is literally the claim's subject (llm.hallucination), so there is no cross-species or cross-task transfer to discount, only the objective-vs-runtime level mismatch already charged against mapping fidelity.
